# slate-kv-ffi

[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20OR%20Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](#license)

**The stable C ABI for [SLATE](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate).** A `cdylib` + `staticlib` over [`slate-kv`](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/tree/main/crates/slate-kv), with a `slate.h` generated by cbindgen at build time. Every non-Rust integration — the [Go binding](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/tree/main/bind/go) and any future one — sits on this surface.

Not published to crates.io: it is a build artifact, not a dependency. You link the library, you do not `cargo add` it.

## Build

```sh
make ffi-staticlib          # cargo build -p slate-kv-ffi --release
```

Produces:

| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Header | `crates/slate-kv-ffi/include/slate.h` |
| Static library | `target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.a` |
| Shared library | `target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.{so,dylib,dll}` |

`slate.h` is **generated** — it is written by `build.rs` on every build. Edit the Rust signatures and doc comments, never the header.

Rust static libraries do not bundle system libraries, so a static link needs the platform's link flags. Ask the toolchain rather than guessing:

```sh
make ffi-native-libs        # prints the exact --print native-static-libs output
```

Typical results: macOS `-liconv -lSystem -lc -lm`; Linux/glibc `-lgcc_s -lutil -lrt -lpthread -lm -ldl -lc`.

## Hello world

```c
#include "slate.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void) {
    // Refuse to run against a header from a different ABI generation.
    if ((slate_abi_version() >> 16) != SLATE_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR) {
        fprintf(stderr, "slate ABI mismatch\n");
        return 1;
    }

    uint8_t key[32] = {0x42};           // 32 bytes, exactly
    slate_options opts = {
        .capacity_bytes = 4u * 1024 * 1024,
        .max_keys       = 8192,
        .b_commit       = 0,            // 0 => auto: engine computes B* itself
        .theta          = 16384,
        .profile        = SLATE_PROFILE_PI,
    };

    slate_db *db = NULL;
    int rc = slate_open("./slate_db", key, &opts, &db);   // path is a DIRECTORY
    if (rc != SLATE_OK) {
        char msg[256];
        slate_last_error_message(NULL, msg, sizeof msg);  // NULL db => open-time error
        fprintf(stderr, "open failed (%d): %s\n", rc, msg);
        return 1;
    }
    memset(key, 0, sizeof key);         // the engine has derived what it needs

    slate_put_durable(db, (const uint8_t *)"k1", 2, (const uint8_t *)"v1", 2);

    uint8_t buf[64];
    size_t len = sizeof buf;
    if (slate_get(db, (const uint8_t *)"k1", 2, buf, &len) == SLATE_OK) {
        printf("%.*s\n", (int)len, buf);
    }

    slate_close(db);                    // commits best-effort, then frees the handle
    return 0;
}
```

Compile and link:

```sh
# Substitute the flags printed by `make ffi-native-libs` for <native-libs>.
cc example.c -Icrates/slate-kv-ffi/include \
   target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.a <native-libs> -o example
```

## API

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `slate_abi_version()` | `(major << 16) \| minor`. Check before anything else. |
| `slate_open(path, key, opts, out)` | `path` is a directory; `key` is exactly 32 bytes. Writes the handle to `*out`; `*out` is set to `NULL` first. |
| `slate_put(db, k, klen, v, vlen)` | Buffered. **Not durable yet.** |
| `slate_put_durable(db, k, klen, v, vlen)` | Put + commit. Durable on return. |
| `slate_get(db, k, klen, v_out, vlen_inout)` | See the two-call pattern below. |
| `slate_delete(db, k, klen)` | Buffered, like `slate_put`. |
| `slate_commit(db)` | The acknowledgement point. |
| `slate_compact(db)` | One GC pass. |
| `slate_security_mode(db)` | `0` = Full, `1` = BestEffortRollback, `2` = NoRollbackProtection, `-1` = error. |
| `slate_close(db)` | Best-effort commit, then frees. The handle is dangling afterwards. |
| `slate_last_error_message(db, buf, len)` | NUL-terminated detail for the last failure. Pass `db = NULL` to read an `slate_open` failure. |

### Return codes

| Code | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SLATE_OK` | 0 | Success |
| `SLATE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` | -1 | Key absent (a normal result, not a failure) |
| `SLATE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL` | -2 | `*vlen_inout` now holds the size you need |
| `SLATE_ERR_INVALID_ARG` | -3 | NULL pointer, `klen == 0`, oversized key/value |
| `SLATE_ERR_TAMPERED` | -10 | **The stored data was altered** |
| `SLATE_ERR_ROLLBACK` | -11 | **An older database image was substituted** |
| `SLATE_ERR_INTERNAL` | -99 | A panic was caught at the boundary |
| `SLATE_ERR_IO` | -100 | Underlying I/O failure |

`-10` and `-11` must reach a human. They are not retryable, and a binding that maps them onto a generic error type has removed the feature people chose SLATE for.

### The `slate_get` two-call pattern

```c
size_t len = 0;
int rc = slate_get(db, k, klen, NULL, &len);      /* 1. ask for the size  */
if (rc == SLATE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL) {
    uint8_t *buf = malloc(len);
    rc = slate_get(db, k, klen, buf, &len);       /* 2. fetch into it     */
    /* ... */
    free(buf);
}
```

`vlen_inout` is in/out: on entry it is your buffer's capacity, on return it is the value's true length — set even when the buffer was too small, which is what makes the sizing call work. `SLATE_ERR_NOT_FOUND` leaves nothing written.

Ownership is simple by construction: **the library never allocates memory that the caller must free.** Values are copied into your buffer; the only owned object is the `slate_db *` handle, released by `slate_close`.

## Boundary guarantees

- **No unwinding across the ABI.** Every entry point wraps its body in `catch_unwind`; a panic becomes `SLATE_ERR_INTERNAL`.
- **NULL is checked, not assumed.** Every pointer argument is validated before use; a bad one returns `SLATE_ERR_INVALID_ARG`.
- **Bytes, not strings.** Keys and values are arbitrary bytes with explicit lengths, never NUL-terminated. Only `path` is a C string (UTF-8).
- **Errors are per-handle.** Each `slate_db` owns a mutex-guarded last-error string, so two threads on two handles cannot clobber each other's message. Open-time failures use a thread-local, which is why `slate_last_error_message(NULL, …)` is the right call there.

Caller obligations that no signature can express: never pass a NULL pointer with a zero length (use a valid dummy address), never use a handle after `slate_close`, and serialise calls on one handle under your own lock.

## Testing

```sh
cc crates/slate-kv-ffi/tests/ffi_smoke.c -Icrates/slate-kv-ffi/include \
   target/release/libslate_kv_ffi.a <native-libs> -o /tmp/ffi_smoke && /tmp/ffi_smoke

make bind-test      # runs the Go binding's conformance suite against this library
```

## Writing a new binding

Read [`bind/README.md`](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/blob/main/bind/README.md) for the rules every binding follows and [`bind/CONFORMANCE.md`](https://github.com/ja7ad/slate/blob/main/bind/CONFORMANCE.md) for the suite it must pass. In short: stay a thin translation layer, derive constants from the generated header, verify `slate_abi_version()` on open, and keep tamper/rollback as distinct types in the host language.
